facts.claim: Social media addiction is formalized as entrapment in an engineered wrong attractor built through intentional variable-ratio reinforcement design.
facts.quote: We apply the Displacement Framework to social media addiction, formalizing it as entrapment in an engineered wrong attractor built through intentional variable-ratio reinforcement design.

facts.claim: The design of compulsion loops by attention engineers is ethically equivalent to designing addictive products like tobacco.
facts.quote: The intentional design of compulsion loops by attention engineers is analyzed as ethically equivalent to designing addictive products, with tobacco regulation as historical precedent.

facts.claim: Infinite scrolling replaces deep interpersonal relations with fragmented, ephemeral interactions.
facts.quote: It replaces deep, sustained interpersonal relations with fragmented, ephemeral interactions, mediated by algorithmic infrastructures optimized for retention rather than human connection.

facts.claim: Digital addiction is an overarching concept that is closely related to scrolling syndrome.
facts.quote: This was done as digital addiction is an overarching concept in relation to scrolling syndrome and closely related to the same.

facts.claim: Scrolling syndrome shares common criteria with other clinical disorders.
facts.quote: Even for other clinical disorders, common criteria shared with scrolling syndrome have been listed as clinical markers

facts.claim: Infinite scrolling immerses users in algorithmic loops that are difficult to break because there are no natural stopping points.
facts.quote: By continuously loading content without natural stopping points (e. g. the end of the page), infinite scrolling immerses users in algorithmic loops that are difficult to break.

research.angle: Infinite scrolling uses intentional variable-ratio reinforcement design to create compulsion loops that replace deep human connection with fragmented interactions.
research.verdict: The sources indicate that infinite scrolling is a deliberate design choice that creates difficult-to-break loops and shares clinical markers with other addictions.
research.caveat: One source is a preprint that has not yet been peer-reviewed.
